clue.text: Left Elizabeth's favourite cheese

parts.note: red is the colour of the political left, so a leftist is a red
Robert Dudley, Earl of Leicester, was the favourite courtier of Queen Elizabeth I

explanation.surface: A cheese once loved by a queen has been left behind.
explanation.walkthrough: RED LEICESTER is an orange English cheese from Leicestershire.
explanation.definitionFit: Red Leicester is a hard English variety of cow's-milk dairy product.

clue.text: Judge about to release one finally put inside

parts.note: re is a Latin-derived word for concerning or about

indicators.note: put inside tells us the last letter of one goes into the word for release

parts.note: to release a captive is to set them free

indicators.note: finally picks out the closing letter of the word one

explanation.surface: A judge is about to free a prisoner, but one ends up jailed after all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Judge' could be a verb, but here it is the official who rules on a match; 'finally' takes the last letter of 'one'.
explanation.definitionFit: A referee is an umpire or arbiter who rules on disputes, as a judge does.

clue.text: Professional who may draw out wisdom

definitions.text: Professional who may draw out wisdom

parts.words: Professional who may draw out wisdom
parts.note: reads like a teacher drawing knowledge from a pupil, but the wisdom is a wisdom tooth, extracted by a tooth doctor

explanation.definitionFit: A dentist is the medical practitioner who extracts teeth, including wisdom teeth.

clue.text: Pepper is greener when developed

indicators.note: developed suggests something worked up into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Talk of a pepper turning greener as it ripens on the vine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pepper' looks like the vegetable, but it means something that peps you up.
explanation.definitionFit: One who peps things up gives a boost of vigour, as a tonic or stimulant does.

clue.text: Closely scrutinised in cabinet

definitions.meaning: burglars case a joint when they inspect it carefully before a robbery
something put away in a display case or cupboard is encased

explanation.definitionFit: Casing a building means inspecting it beforehand, and an item stored in a box or cabinet is enclosed in it.

clue.text: Poet with touch of sycophancy writes on Queen Elizabeth

indicators.note: a touch of something is just a little of it, here its opening letter

parts.note: a writer pens words
ER is the royal cipher, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A court poet flatters the queen with fawning verses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' just sets the pieces in order: S, then PENS, then ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Edmund Spenser was the Elizabethan author of The Faerie Queene, a verse epic.

clue.text: Some xeroxed it in general, preparing copy

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An office worker photocopied documents generally while getting copy ready.
explanation.definitionFit: Editing is revising and correcting text so it is ready for publication.

clue.text: Spy strongly funny comic hit that's zany

definitions.text: Spy strongly funny comic hit that's zany

indicators.note: zany means crazily eccentric, so the preceding words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A comedy show hailed as a madcap smash, strongly funny with spies in it.
explanation.walkthrough: All five words from 'Spy' to 'hit' are fodder; the whole clue also describes the anarchic BBC sketch show.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1969-74 BBC sketch series was a famously surreal, zany comedy hit.

clue.text: Crime characterised by receiver

parts.note: of can mean having the quality of, as in a man of honour
a fence is a receiver of stolen goods

explanation.surface: A crime is defined by who ends up receiving the loot.
explanation.definitionFit: An offence is a breach of law, a criminal act.

clue.text: One Clapton hit has explosive guitar figure

parts.note: has contracts to 's, giving S
HE is short for high explosive
a riff is a repeated phrase played on guitar

explanation.surface: A Clapton single features an explosive guitar riff.
explanation.walkthrough: Eric Clapton's hit was 'I Shot the Sheriff', so the lawman is literally one he hit, shot in the song.
explanation.definitionFit: In Clapton's song 'I Shot the Sheriff', the county lawman is the one gunned down.

clue.text: See 7
Go to bed before middle of night, being deviant

parts.note: to turn in is to retire for the night

indicators.note: middle of picks out the central letter of the word night

explanation.surface: Someone who sleeps through midnight is somehow being unconventional.
explanation.definitionFit: Turning means veering or deviating from a straight course.

clue.text: Refuse to accept its preposterous fate

indicators.note: to accept means to take in, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: to refuse a request is to deny it

indicators.note: preposterous literally means before-behind, back to front, so its letters are read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to accept that their fate is absurd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'preposterous' (literally before-behind) makes STI from 'its'; 'to accept' puts that inside the word for refuse.
explanation.definitionFit: Destiny is the predetermined course of events, one's lot.

clue.text: Tuck taking dish finally to heart

indicators.note: finally to heart says the final letter shifts into the centre of the word

parts.note: a plate is a dish for serving food

explanation.surface: A diner tucks in, taking a dish and finally getting to the heart of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tuck' looks like eating, but it is a fold in fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleat is a fold sewn into cloth, as a tuck is.

clue.text: Endless vote to get a new bishop

indicators.note: Endless means the final letter is dropped from the word for vote

parts.note: suffrage is the right to vote, or a vote

explanation.surface: An election without end produces a newly appointed bishop.
explanation.definitionFit: A suffragan is an assistant cleric who helps a diocesan prelate.

clue.text: Wilts river to which a standard may be set

definitions.text: to which a standard may be set

parts.note: plants that wilt are said to flag
the Taff is a river flowing through Cardiff in Wales

explanation.surface: A Wiltshire river by which some standard may be set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wilts' looks like the abbreviation for Wiltshire, an English county, but it is a verb. A standard here is a banner.
explanation.definitionFit: A flagstaff is the pole on which a banner or ensign is hoisted.

clue.text: Expose outlandish skill around eating place

indicators.note: around means turned round, so the joined pieces read backwards

parts.note: to air something is to expose it
OTT, over the top, means extravagantly outlandish
art is a skill, as in the art of conversation

explanation.surface: Displaying bizarre talent at a restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: One reversal, signalled by 'around', turns all three joined pieces, which read RIATTOTRA forwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A trattoria is an informal Italian restaurant.

clue.text: A defeat of king over ancient city one is not rewarded

parts.note: mate in chess is the defeat of the king
Ur was an ancient Sumerian city

explanation.surface: A king's defeat in an ancient city goes unrewarded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' places A and MATE above UR in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: An amateur takes part without pay, unlike a professional.

clue.text: Fundamentalist — his end: prohibition on alcoholic drink

annotationWithheld.clue: Fundamentalist — his end: prohibition on alcoholic drink

clue.text: Boy in charge of acoustics

parts.note: a boy is someone's son

explanation.surface: A lad is put in charge of the sound system.
explanation.definitionFit: Sonic means relating to sound waves, the subject of the science of sound.

clue.text: Like Brighton beach, hard to enter one at a time

indicators.note: to enter means to go into, so this letter is placed within the other word

parts.note: singly means one by one
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Brighton's beach is hard to get onto, one person at a time.
explanation.walkthrough: Brighton, a resort on England's south coast, has a pebbly beach.
explanation.definitionFit: Shingly means covered with pebbles, as that seaside resort's shore is.

clue.text: Turning up in Israeli port a northern girl

indicators.note: turning up in a down clue means the pieces read from bottom to top

parts.note: Eilat is Israel's port on the Red Sea

explanation.surface: A northern girl turns up in an Israeli port.
explanation.definitionFit: Natalie is a female given name.

clue.text: They prophesy of Greek hero-not he

parts.note: o' is a shortened form of of, as in will-o'-the-wisp

indicators.note: not tells us to remove the word he from the hero's name

parts.note: Heracles is the Greek form of Hercules

explanation.surface: Prophets speak of a Greek hero, insisting it was not him.
explanation.definitionFit: Oracles were seers at Greek shrines who foretold the future.

clue.text: Composer with South American connection

parts.note: a tie is a link or bond

explanation.surface: A composer with ties to South America.
explanation.definitionFit: Erik Satie was a French musician who wrote the Gymnopedies.

clue.text: Note with one sorting out a quick one

indicators.note: with here means holding, so the letter for note sits inside

parts.note: a sifter separates or sorts material
n. is the abbreviation for note, as in a footnote reference

explanation.surface: Someone sorting out notes pauses for a quick drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a quick one' is a quick drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A snifter is a small alcoholic drink, a tot.

clue.text: Sweet, mint perhaps in place

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to place something is to set it down
mint is an example of a herb

explanation.surface: Something sweet, perhaps mint, in its place.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherbet is a fizzy powdered confection.

clue.text: One supporting financially Oxford University woman of erudition

parts.note: an angel is a financial backer, especially of a theatre production

explanation.surface: A benefactor at Oxford University is a learned woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Maya Angelou was an American poet and memoirist celebrated for her learning.

clue.text: Description of Pericles employing perfect irony

indicators.note: employing suggests the letters are put to use in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Pericles is described with consummate irony.
explanation.walkthrough: Pericles, Prince of Tyre is a Shakespeare play; 'Pericles' looks like the Athenian statesman.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's title gives the hero as ruler of the Phoenician city of Tyre.
